sections.title: Mission · Recognize Linux Hardware
paragraphs: Linux runs on hardware. Recognize major computer components and understand how Linux represents storage devices.

sections.title: Motherboard
paragraphs: The motherboard is the main system board connecting the CPU, memory, storage controllers, expansion devices, and other components.

sections.title: Processor
paragraphs: The processor, or CPU, executes instructions and performs the central computation used by the operating system and applications.

sections.title: Power Supply
paragraphs: The power supply unit converts and supplies electrical power to the computer's components.

sections.title: Optical Drives
paragraphs: Optical drives read or write disc-based media such as CDs and DVDs.

sections.title: Peripherals
paragraphs: A peripheral is an external or additional connected device such as a keyboard, mouse, printer, or removable storage device.
sections.callout: PERIPHERAL = DEVICE CONNECTED TO THE COMPUTER

sections.title: Hard Disk Drives
paragraphs: An HDD provides persistent mechanical storage using spinning magnetic media.

sections.title: Solid-State Drives
paragraphs: An SSD provides persistent flash-based storage without spinning platters.

sections.title: Partitions
paragraphs: A partition is a logical subdivision of a physical storage device. One disk can contain multiple partitions.

sections.title: Linux Device Files
paragraphs: Linux exposes many hardware devices through special files under /dev/. Programs interact with those device-file paths.
sections.callout: HARDWARE CAN BE REPRESENTED THROUGH DEVICE FILES

sections.title: /dev/sd*
paragraphs: Names such as /dev/sda identify storage devices, while /dev/sda1 identifies a partition on that device. Additional disks can be /dev/sdb and so on.

sections.title: Exam Trap · Disk vs. Partition
sections.callout: DISK = sda · PIECE OF DISK = sda1

sections.title: Drivers
paragraphs: A driver is software that enables the operating system to communicate with and control hardware.

sections.title: Why Drivers Matter
paragraphs: Without a suitable driver, the operating system may not recognize a device or may not use all of its features. Drivers translate between OS operations and device behavior.
